newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps weaken late.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps weaken late.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed, with Standard & Poor's 500s weakening late after end-of-month buying failed to materialize as some traders had expected, floor analysts said.
March S&Ps rose above 797.00 and towards the daily high of 797.80 late in the day, but found little buying interest.

"Pit traders were all set up, looking for buys, and then we hit sell programs," one floor analyst said. Arbitrage sell programs, which occurred earlier in the session, were hit in the last half-hour of trade at a premium of 0.95 over the cash S&P index.
Sell-stop orders were particularly heavy at the 795.00 level, which fueled March S&Ps' decline below 791.00 in the final minutes of trade.
In addition, March began trading at a discount to the cash index. For most of the day, March traded slightly above fair value, which was quoted by several traders at 1.30 to 1.50 points above cash.

"They've been closing on the cheap side for the last three days," one S&P futures analyst said, adding that March had lost its premium near the close for three days in a row. "It's somewhat of a negative sign when the market does that."

He said S&P futures' tendency to sell off below the cash S&P price following U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday pointed to further declines next week.
Traders and analysts pegged support at 785.00, 782.00 and 780.00.
"We went through these levels (on the upside) so quickly, it's hard to determine where support will come in," he said. "But we may have to probe lower."
He said Greenspan's comments had shaken the market's confidence.
Greenspan said Wednesday he couldn't rule out a pre-emptive tightening, and also said caution was warranted in U.S. stocks as the market's rise was unsustainable.
His comments on the stock market were similar to his statement about "irrational exuberance" last December, traders noted.
Greenspan's testimony will continue on Wednesday, March 5.
Nikkei futures remained sharply lower on follow-through selling from overnight trade in Tokyo. Profit-taking in some export-oriented Japanese companies was attributed to fiscal year-end pressures.

At the end of pit trade, March S&P 500s were down 2.10 points at 790.40, KCBT Value Lines fell 3.40 to 705.10, Nikkei lost 495.0 to 18,490.0, Midcap was steady at 261.80, NYSE Composite was off 1.25 to 415.00, Russell rose 1.70 to 359.80, and Nasdaq 100s were up 1.75 at 848.50.
